components.detail: Checked on 25 Oct 2026: 70 C flow while charging the cylinder, system pressure 1.9 bar. Healthy pressure range is 0.8 to 3.0 bar.
components.how: The boiler heats water in a sealed circuit and sends it where the controller asks: to the radiators, to the underfloor loops, or through a coil inside the Megaflo cylinder to heat the stored tap water. On its display, a tap symbol means it is heating the water tank; a radiator symbol means it is heating the house.
label: Boiler
Vaillant 637
components.name: Boiler
components.what: A Vaillant ecoTEC plus 637 system boiler. It burns gas and makes hot water for the heating system. It is the single heat source for the whole house.

components.detail: Seen on 25 Oct 2026: room 20.5 C, outside 9.5 C, desired heating temperature 24.0 C, controller clock showing 5:46 at 8:03 real time.
components.how: It runs heating and hot water to a daily timetable stored in its own clock. Hot water modes: Auto follows the timetable, Day keeps the tank hot all the time. Cylinder boost heats the tank once, right away, outside the timetable, then cancels itself. Because its clock runs about 2 hours 16 minutes slow, every timed programme fires late by that much.
label: Controller
VRC 470
components.name: Heating controller
components.what: A Vaillant VRC 470 weather compensator. It is the timetable keeper for heating and hot water, and it adjusts boiler temperature to the weather outside.

components.detail: On the morning of 25 Oct 2026 three baths drained the tank and the timetable had not fired because of the slow controller clock. Setting hot water to Day started the reheat.
components.how: Taps draw stored hot water from the tank. The boiler reheats the tank through a coil inside it, only when the controller timetable or a boost asks. Back to back baths can drain the tank; a full reheat takes about 30 to 45 minutes. The tank also has a 3 kW electric immersion heater as backup, switched off since 10 Oct 2026 to save electricity. Standing heat loss is 1.57 kWh per day.
label: Megaflo cylinder
210 litres
components.name: Megaflo cylinder
components.what: A Heatrae Sadia Megaflo Eco unvented cylinder holding 210 litres of hot water. This tank, not the boiler, is what feeds the taps and baths.

components.detail: This circuit is separate from the underfloor wiring centre, so it kept working during the underfloor power fault.
components.how: When the controller calls for heat, the boiler sends hot water around this circuit. The chrome towel rail is heated by boiler water, not electricity; its heat is set by the valves at its base.
label: Radiators +
towel rails
components.name: Radiators and towel rails
components.what: Radiators in the upper floor rooms, plus heated towel rails in the bathrooms. All of them run on hot water from the gas boiler.

components.how: Hot water rises from the boiler through the radiator circuit. The room thermostat for this floor is the VRC 470 controller itself.
label: Radiator
top bedroom
components.name: Top bedroom radiator
components.what: The radiator in the large top floor bedroom, fed by the same boiler circuit as the other radiators.

components.detail: Checked and off. This was one of the hidden electricity users behind the high summer bills.
components.how: A heating mat under the floor warms the tiles directly. On 10 Oct 2026 it was found switched on in manual mode, set to 23 C with the floor near 29 C, even though it was thought to be off since May. It was switched fully off the same day.
label: Top bathroom
electric floor
components.name: Top-floor bathroom
components.what: A bathroom with electric underfloor heating under the tiles, controlled by its own Comfort Zone thermostat. It uses electricity, not the boiler.

components.detail: One of two bathrooms still to check. Checking takes one minute: the thermostat screen should be dark when off.
components.how: Same system as the top floor bathroom: an electric mat under the tiles. Until its thermostat is checked, nobody knows whether it is off, timed, or quietly running like the top floor one was.
label: Family bathroom
electric floor
components.name: Family bathroom
components.what: The first floor family bathroom, with electric underfloor heating and its own Comfort Zone thermostat.

components.detail: One of two bathrooms still to check, alongside the family bathroom.
components.how: An electric mat under the tiles, independent of the boiler. Its state is unknown until someone looks at its thermostat.
label: En-suite
electric floor
components.name: En-suite bathroom
components.what: The en-suite bathroom, also with electric underfloor heating on its own thermostat.

components.detail: There are two consumer units in the cupboard. Both were fully on during the underfloor investigation.
components.how: Labels include Sockets Under Stairs, Boiler, Cylinder, and the ring circuits for each floor. On 24 Oct 2026 every breaker was photographed on, which proved the underfloor fault was not a tripped breaker.
label: Consumer unit
fuse box
components.name: Consumer unit
components.what: The house fuse box. Every circuit in the house takes its power through here, each with its own breaker switch.

components.detail: Fault state on 24 Oct 2026: POWER light dark, every zone light dark, the Drayton LP711 timer beside it also blank, while every consumer unit breaker was on. Fix is an electrician visit.
components.how: When a thermostat calls for heat, this box powers open that zone's actuator valve, starts the manifold pump and asks the boiler for heat. Its valves are normally shut, so with no power nothing can flow. Its board fuse is a 5 amp anti-surge 20 mm glass fuse, currently stuck fast in its clips. The Zone 4 pump control switch was found set to NO and was moved to YES on 24 Oct 2026, which is correct for underfloor heating, but the box still has no power.
label: Wiring centre
Polypipe UFH4ZW
components.name: Underfloor wiring centre
components.what: A Polypipe UFH4ZW wiring centre. It is the brain of the ground floor underfloor heating: it listens to the room thermostats and opens the valves on the manifold.

components.detail: Pump green light on, flow gauges near zero on all four loops, 24 Oct 2026.
components.how: The pump pushes warm water around the loops under the floor. The mixing valve blends the water down to a gentle floor temperature. Each loop has a flow gauge and a valve motor (actuator) opened by the wiring centre. Loop 2 has a plain manual cap instead of a motor, so it has no automatic control. With the wiring centre dead, the pump runs but the valves stay shut and all four gauges read near zero.
label: UFH manifold
pump + 4 loops
components.name: Underfloor manifold and pump
components.what: The pipe hub for the floor heating: two brass bars, four floor loops, a Grundfos UPS2 25-40/60 pump, a thermostatic mixing valve and four flow gauges.

components.detail: The lobby target was raised to 20 C by hand on 24 Oct 2026 while family are staying.
components.how: Each thermostat watches its zone and asks the wiring centre for heat when the room is below target. On 24 Oct 2026 the living hall sat at 18 C against targets above 20 C, calling correctly, but the dead wiring centre could not act on the calls.
label: Thermostats x3
lobby, hall x2
components.name: Underfloor thermostats

status.label: Working, but their calls go nowhere

components.what: Three Polypipe room thermostats for the floor zones: one in the entry lobby and two in the living hall, one for each half of the big room.

components.detail: This is the visible symptom of the wiring centre power fault, not a fault in the floor itself.
components.how: Warm water flowing through the loops turns the whole floor into a slow, gentle radiator. A working loop feels warm underfoot. Right now no water can enter the loops because the manifold valves are held shut by the dead wiring centre, so the floor stays cold and the living hall stalls near 20 C.
label: Floor loops x4
lobby + living hall
components.name: Floor loops
components.what: Four loops of pipe buried in the ground floor screed: one for the entry lobby and the rest across the open-plan living hall.

components.detail: Same electrician visit as the wiring centre. The manual is saved in Drive under Household, Manuals.
components.how: It is faulty: it powers up, runs for 3 to 4 minutes, then goes completely dark. The likely cause is a plug, fuse or connection failing as it warms under load, or an overheat cut-out tripping. It uses almost no electricity in this state (about 0.2 kWh per short run), so it is not a bill problem. It is left switched off at the wall; restarting it repeatedly is not safe.
label: Dimplex Quantum
storage heater
components.name: Dimplex Quantum storage heater
components.what: A Dimplex Quantum electric storage heater on the utility room wall. It stores heat in bricks and releases it through the day.

components.how: It heats water only while that tap runs, so it is a small, occasional load. It is not connected to the main hot water system.
label: Instant heater
utility sink
components.name: Instant water heater
components.what: A small instant electric water heater under the utility room sink.

components.detail: The display history is now the easiest way to watch the house: a normal day without car charging lands near 12 to 15 kWh of electricity.
components.how: Tariffs shown on the display: electricity 26.613p per kWh plus 51.83p per day; gas 7.91p per kWh plus 29.33p per day. From 1 to 24 Oct 2026 the house used 367 kWh of electricity (about 15.3 kWh a day) and 467 kWh of gas (about 19.5 kWh a day). Every cost screen on the display reconciles exactly with these tariffs.
label: Smart meters
E.ON + IHD
components.name: Smart meters and display
components.room: Meter boxes and the SmartView 3 display
components.what: Smart meters for gas and electricity, fitted around the end of September 2026, with a SmartView 3 in-home display that shows live use, daily history and costs.

components.detail: The car covers about 3,000 miles a year, so charging is occasional, not daily.
components.how: It takes power from the grid through the consumer unit and charges the car at home. A charging session adds roughly 10 to 20 kWh to the day's electricity, which is why some days look high on the meter display.
label: Wall Connector
Tesla
components.name: Tesla Wall Connector
components.what: The Tesla Wall Connector in the garage, the home charger for the car.

components.detail: Charging days are the main reason daily electricity swings between about 13 and 22 kWh.
components.how: Charged at home from the Wall Connector. In the energy picture it is the single biggest occasional load in the house.
label: Tesla Model Y
components.name: Tesla Model Y
components.what: A Tesla Model Y Long Range, rear wheel drive, leased.

scenarios.caption: Floor: warm · Tank: hot · Radiators: on · Car: charging
explanation: A normal day. The boiler heats the house and keeps the tank hot on the controller timetable.
Warm water runs through the floor loops and the radiators. The car charges when it is plugged in, which is the main reason some days use more electricity.
Even on a normal day, two things stay as they are until fixed: the Dimplex is faulty and off, and the two first floor bathroom floors are still unchecked.
scenarios.name: Normal day

scenarios.caption: Tank: drained, then reheating · Boiler: busy with the tank · Floor: warm
explanation: Three baths back to back drain the 210 litre tank, because taps use stored water, not instant heat from the boiler. This is normal, not a breakdown.
Cylinder boost then points the boiler at the tank alone until it is hot again: about 30 to 45 minutes for a full reheat. House heating pauses while the tank charges.
The immersion heater could reheat the tank with electricity instead, but it stays off to save money.
scenarios.name: Morning baths

scenarios.caption: Floor: cold · Tank: hot · Radiators: on · Controller clock: slow
explanation: Today, 25 October 2026: the underfloor wiring centre has no power, so its valves stay shut, no water enters the floor loops, and the living hall stalls near 20 C with a cold floor.
The boiler, radiators and hot water run on a separate path and are unaffected. The manifold pump still runs, but it only stirs water inside the manifold.
Separately, the controller clock runs about 2 hours 16 minutes slow, which is why the hot water timetable fired late this morning and the tank ran cold after the baths.
